content: I have now approved PNT#774 to import LeanCert into the project for verified numerical tasks, such as numerical integration. However, we are moving certain computationally intensive LeanCert verifications (such as numerical upper and lower bounds on li 2) outside of the main PNT+ lean files to avoid excessive build times. The initial building of LeanCert may take some time, but hopefully this will only need to be done once per mathlib bump. Please let me know if there are any issues with excessively slow build times, or other issues related to this.

It seems like that LeanCert can't really deal with inequalities involving the ceiling function, as shown in my PR: PNT#980. In this PR I want to show the following two inequalities:

import Mathlib

example : ⌈Real.exp 59⌉₊ + 4 ≤ 11325 * 10 ^ 22 := by sorry

example : ⌈Real.exp 60⌉₊ + 4 ≤ 7785131284000000000000000004 := by sorry

These two goals can't be automatically solved by interval_decide, so instead I first proved the following two inequalities:

import Mathlib

example : Real.exp 59 + 4 + 1 ≤ 11325 * 10 ^ 22 := by sorry -- solved by interval_decide

example : Real.exp 60 + 4 + 1 ≤ 7785131284000000000000000004 := by sorry -- solved by interval_decide

This might be something LeanCert could improve. Nevertheless, I am still quite impressed by this one-tactic proof of Real.exp 59 + 4 + 1 ≤ 11325 * 10 ^ 22 produced by LeanCert.

Added Nat.ceil preprocessing in interval_decide: goals like ⌈e⌉₊ + k ≤ n are reduced to a real inequality (e ≤ n - k), then closed via Nat.ceil_le + omega.

So with LeanCert’s tactic import, these should now solve with a single interval_decide.

Summary of changes since the last pinned version:

  • Chebyshev psi engine (ChebyshevPsi.lean): certified ψ(N) upper bounds via incremental von Mangoldt accumulation, generalized to arbitrary slopes. All bridge theorems fully proved.
  • Dyadic backend optimizations: binary exponentiation, sign-based multiplication, Horner evaluation. Dyadic-first dispatch with inv/log fallback.
  • interval_decide Nat.ceil support: handles goals involving ⌈e⌉₊ (used in PNT#980).
  • Expression reification: added abs, max, min, rational-exponent rpow.
  • Warning fixes contributed by @ajirving.

The general pattern for enumeration-based bounds: define a computable Bool checker, prove a bridge theorem ("if checker returns true, the math holds"), then native_decide runs it at native speed.

The same approach could apply to other numerical verification tasks in the project, if the check is expressible as a decidable Bool computation, LeanCert can likely handle it

There is a certain amount of python code in the LeanCert repository. What precisely is the interaction between Lean and Python in LeanCert? Is there any lean code that externally runs a Python script, for instance?

No Lean code calls Python. The Python SDK is a discovery frontend: explore functions, find bounds, locate extrema interactively (lc.find_bounds(...), lc.verify_bound(...)), then write the actual Lean proof using the constants you found.

The workflow is "explore in Python → prove in Lean." The SDK calls a compiled Lean binary under the hood, none of it is in the import path or proof chain
I wonder if splitting the repository into a pure lean one, and as downstream one for the python library would help here.
That makes sense, will get it done this week!

I apologize if this is not the right place to post this, but I'm running into an issue while formalizing corollary 22 of FKS2, interval_decide works on ⊢ 2.5 ≤ 9.2211 * (5.0 * √5.0) * rexp (-0.8476 * √10.0) ~ 7.066
but failed on ⊢ 2.5 ≤ 9.2211 * rexp (-0.8476 * √1.5) ~ 3.2655. You can see using these two examples

import PrimeNumberTheoremAnd.FKS2
lemma interval_decide_fail : (2.5 : ℝ) ≤ 9.2211 * Real.exp (-0.8476 * Real.sqrt 1.5) := by
  interval_decide  -- FAILS

lemma interval_decide_success : (2.5 : ℝ) ≤ 9.2211 * (5.0 * Real.sqrt 5.0) * Real.exp (-0.8476 * Real.sqrt 10.0) := by
  interval_decide  -- OK

Is there some way around this issue ? Or should I not use interval_decide here ?

Thanks for letting me know. This was a LeanCert interval_decide issue. The tactic was normalizing the closed expression too early: norm_num rewrote sqrt 1.5 into a quotient form like √3 / √2, which made the later dyadic interval certificate too weak/harder.

I’ve merged a fix to LeanCert main: interval_decide now tries the closed-expression certificate path before that normalization step. With the fix, your original example works directly:

lemma interval_decide_fail :
       (2.5 : ℝ) ≤ 9.2211 * Real.exp (-0.8476 * Real.sqrt 1.5) := by
     interval_decide

Once PNT updates toolchain & LeanCert dep to 4.29.1 you should be able to do prove it this way. A temporary workaround is to insert the rational bound sqrt 1.5 ≤ 5 / 4 and use monotonicity of Real.exp.

Sharing here since this seems adjacent enough to PNT

I’ve merged a new analytic-number-theory certificate layer into LeanCert. It is on the LeanCert side now, and should become available in PNT once the dependency updates to Lean 4.29.1 / the newer LeanCert revision.

The new modules add reusable “checker → bridge theorem” infrastructure for finite ANT-style certification workflows, including:

  • finite step-sum certificates
  • exact Abel / partial-summation transforms,
  • bounded Abel certificates from prefix envelopes,
  • finite Euler-product and log-product certificates,
  • finite Dirichlet-style weighted sums,
  • prime Euler-product presets,
  • finite Mertens-style prime-sum certificates,
  • reusable rational interval combinators.

They follow the usual LeanCert Golden Theorem pattern: computable checkers paired with semantic verify_* bridge theorems.

Examples of the new API shape include:

verify_abel_interval
verify_eulerProduct_interval
verify_dirichletSum_interval
verify_mertensLogSum_interval
verify_mertensAbel_interval

There is also a small certified q-product / product-integral framework:

import LeanCert.QProduct

It supports:

  • exact rational finite evaluations,
  • stability lemmas,
  • certified prime-truncation bounds for product integrals of the form
F S = ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..1, ∏ n ∈ S, (1 - u ^ n)

The q-product component implements the finite product-integral invariant framework developed in the accompanying preprint:

https://zenodo.org/records/20385171

In particular, LeanCert now includes:

  • the finite exact subset-sum evaluator,
  • the prime-indexed directed-limit example primeLambda,
  • certified rational sandwich bounds such as:
(1 / 2 : ℝ) < primeLambda

Docs:

  • ANT API: https://docs.leancert.io/ant/
  • Golden Theorems / architecture: https://docs.leancert.io/architecture/golden-theorems/#analytic-number-theory-bridges
  • QProduct: https://docs.leancert.io/qproduct/
